description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing normal lung fields and mediastinum.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph showing clear lung fields with no visible consolidation, effusion, or masses. The mediastinum appears normal in width, and the heart size is within normal limits. The bony structures, including the ribs, clavicles, and spine, are intact without obvious abnormalities. No foreign devices or pathologic findings are evident.

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing abnormal opacities in the right lung field.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph demonstrating the thorax. There is an area of increased opacity in the right mid to lower lung field, suggestive of consolidation or infiltrate. The cardiac silhouette and mediastinal structures appear within normal limits. The left lung field appears clear. No obvious pleural effusion or pneumothorax is visible. Bony structures, including the ribs and clavicles, appear intact.
visible_findings: increased opacity in the right mid to lower lung field
no visible pleural effusion or pneumothorax

Case_07028/figure3.jpg.source_caption: CT scan of the chest, high resolution.

description.short_caption: High-resolution CT scan of the chest showing bilateral lung abnormalities.
description.detailed_description: This is a high-resolution axial CT scan of the chest. The image demonstrates diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities and interlobular septal thickening, particularly in the lower lung zones. The heart and central mediastinal structures appear normal in size and position. The findings are suggestive of a diffuse interstitial lung process, potentially consistent with an infectious or inflammatory etiology.

Case_07028/figure4.jpg.source_caption: CT scan of the chest, with portion magnified.

description.short_caption: CT scan of the chest showing bilateral lung abnormalities with a magnified portion.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT scan of the chest demonstrates bilateral lung abnormalities, including diffuse ground-glass opacities and areas of consolidation. A magnified portion highlights the fine details of the abnormalities, which are distributed throughout both lungs. The mediastinum and heart are visible in the center, and no significant pleural effusion is noted. The findings suggest a diffuse pulmonary process, potentially infectious or inflammatory in nature.

Case_07028/figure5.jpg.source_caption: DFA of an induced sputum specimen.

description.short_caption: Direct fluorescent antibody (DFA) staining of an induced sputum specimen.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a fluorescent microscopy view of an induced sputum specimen stained with a direct fluorescent antibody (DFA) technique. The bright green fluorescence indicates the presence of a target organism or antigen, surrounded by a darker background. The red and black areas represent unstained or non-fluorescent regions. The DFA technique is commonly used for detecting specific pathogens in clinical specimens.
visible_findings: dark background with red and black areas
fluorescence indicative of a specific antigen or organism
